title: The Black and Tan Orchestra in Los Angeles
summary: Garland names the members of the Black and Tan Orchestra, the leading Los Angeles house band, which played dances and entertainments.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Uh-huh. Now, in -- then you left Orrie for a while to work with the Black and Tan Orchestra.
So you go back to L.A., then.
Black and Tan was right in L.A. See, during that time the Black and Tan was the whole go in Los Angeles.
They had everything, you know. They had little scrap bands around there, but Black and Tan was the whole go (Unintelligible). And they had a good band.
Uh-huh. Any New Orleans players in that band?
No. Had Jack Jackson, was on the piano. He was a friend of Louis.
Leon HERRIFORD was a wonderful saxophone player and violin player.
He's from Kansas City. Paul Holland [Howard:] was a wonderful tenor saxophone player.
Ernest Caycott (Unintelligible) -- was from New Orleans.
Yeah. And Harry Southard was the trombone player. And Leon White was the drummer.
That's right. Yeah. I have a picture over here from about 1915. And that's Black and Tan.
So did you play dances and entertainments still with the same band?
